As fireworks became common, families began joining in with their own favourites, and it became a cherished tradition.

The year Yoimiya took over the family business, Kamisato Ayaka asked her to include the Raiden Shogun's emblem, the Electro Mitsudomoe, because the Shogun would be watching from Tenshukaku. Yoimiya ran launch tubes all over Inazuma City, producing an enormous aerial picture of the city that formed the emblem only when seen from Tenshukaku. This earned her the nickname "Queen of the Summer Festival". Some fifty years ago, the wiki says, Imatani Saburou proposed to his wife at the show.

Story ayaka: In Kamisato Ayaka's Story Quest the Traveler and Ayaka visit a festival on Amakane Island on its final day, as stalls are closing. It is Ayaka's first time ever at a festival, and the vendors, recognising her, stay open longer. They get masks and fortune slips, share a prayer-plaque wish and end the night with Ayaka dancing. Ayaka says she loves festivals' lack of rules, their friendly smiles and carefree happiness. The wiki counts this as the Summer Festival.

Folklore: The Retracing Bolide artifact texts are ghost stories set at a summer festival: a man separated from his parents as a boy during the procession of the divine palanquin, a young man with a stopped pocket watch, and a fox mask and a never-wilting flower. Each describes a beautiful fox-eyed woman who takes someone's hand, offers to watch fireworks, throw darts or play fusen, and disappears. They also mention masks in the likeness of a legendary fox deity, as part of the custom of wearing fox masks.

Scene use: Use the festival for warm, lively evening scenes: bargaining at stalls, children chasing Yoimiya, fortune slips, and the shared hush when a firework rises. It suits first-time festival visitors, reluctant officials seeing normal life, or quiet confessions beneath the display. For strangeness, use the folklore thread: a stranger with fox-like eyes offering the best view.

Keep fireworks associated with Yoimiya's craft: loud, friendly, and quietly sincere. Do not assign a fixed date to the festival, and avoid claiming the Shogun attends in person unless the scene says so.

Status as of 7.1: The show is presented in canon as an ongoing Inazuman tradition with Yoimiya as its star. No source read records a change to the festival after the 2.0 material.

46.content: The Naganohara Fireworks Show is run by Naganohara Fireworks and performed at various Inazuman festivals throughout the year, best seen from Amakane Island over Inazuma City. It began over a century ago as a Yashiro Commission commemoration and grew into a community tradition. Families light fireworks from paper slips, and Yoimiya sets off a grand finale. Her title, Queen of the Summer Festival, comes from the first show she ran, when the emblem of the Raiden Shogun appeared in the sky only from Tenshukaku.

47.content:
Warrior's Spirit Swordfighting Exhibition (also: Warrior's Spirit, Warrior's Spirit Swordfighting Competition, Warrior's Spirit Swordfighting Arena, Archon's Emissary, Emissary of the Archon): The Warrior's Spirit Swordfighting Exhibition is a traditional Inazuman swordsmanship tournament. By legend, the champion earned the honour of crossing swords with the Almighty Shogun herself, with one of her familiars sent to aid and protect the human fighter. Today the Shogun does not attend: the contest ends with an exhibition match in which the champion fights beside a swordsman playing the "Archon's Emissary" against an envoy standing for the Shogun's divine power. The only edition shown in canon was held on Ritou in Version 3.4, hosted by the Yashiro Commission.

The name carries an ideal as much as a sport: the capacity to bear the weight of charity and mercy, and the capability to wield both blade and might. The Shogun is said to have wished to pass on her skill and her will to protect Inazuma's people through martial arts, and the event is presented as a way to spread the elegance of the sword to more people.

The 3.4 edition doubled as a public spectacle with entry tickets, spectators' ballots and a popular figure (Kamisato Ayaka) as its face. In-world this was a deliberate effort by the organisers to widen the audience.

Practice: As Ayaka explains it, the event comes from ancient Inazuman legends in which the martial artist crowned champion was granted a duel with the Almighty Shogun. Since the Shogun was far stronger than any human, the duel would have ended instantly, so she sent a familiar as an emissary who assisted and protected the champion. Later the event became a swordsmanship competition and kept the divine duel as its closing "exhibition match", so that later generations can understand where Warrior's Spirit comes from and what martial arts mean. Today the Shogun sends a special envoy to fight on her behalf. The champion takes the "Martial Artist" role, and the "Divine Familiar" (the Archon's Emissary) is filled by a true swordsman.

Entry in the 3.4 edition was by numbered entry ticket. Madarame Hyakubei of the Kamisato household says applications were so many that every ticket had been issued a week before the event, and describes the contest as both a chance for martial artists to test themselves and a form of honour. The Kono Ittou Art's two disciples, who held a single ticket between them, treated it as so important that they were ready to settle by duel which of them would use it. The vote results were announced on the third day of the competition, and the exhibition match followed the final round.

Regional variation: Rules were relaxed in 3.4. Previously competitors had to practise one of Inazuma's schools of swordsmanship. Onodera of Yae Publishing House, who helped organise the revival, says anyone with a passion for martial arts could now enter, regardless of nationality or status, and weapons were no longer limited to one-handed swords: any close-range weapon within the length and weight requirements was allowed. The field accordingly included a polearm fighter from the desert (Younan) alongside Inazuman swordsmen.

The exhibition match also changed in presentation. In the past the Shogun herself chose what the Archon's Emissary wore; in 3.4, with her support, the choice was handed to the audience. Ayaka notes that in earlier times only the most skilled swordsmen of reputable clans were eligible for the Emissary's role.

Scene use: Use it as a source of pride and rivalry among Inazuma's swordsmen, a conversation topic for anyone who trains with a blade, and a bridge between tradition and a modern, crowd-pleasing show. Inazumans know it as a famous contest with a ceremonial duel at its end, and the Kamisato household and the Kujou are closely tied to its present form.

Keep the tone respectful of the sword arts but friendly: contestants may be earnest to the point of overreaction (the Kono Ittou Art disciples nearly fought each other over one ticket), while organisers worry about spectacle and public opinion. Do not invent winners, past emissaries or a regular calendar. Because the 3.4 edition was a limited-time event, characters who were not there should know the tradition but not the details of that edition.

Examples: The 3.4 edition took place on Ritou in the indoor training area of the Kanjou Commission, hosted by the Yashiro Commission, with Hiiragi Chisato helping with the venue and Onodera of Yae Publishing House planning the event. Its champion was the Traveler. The finale paired the Traveler and Kamisato Ayaka against the Maguu Kengou, presented as the Almighty Shogun's chosen envoy, and they won. Kujou Sara attended on the Shogun's orders to observe and then returned to the Tenshukaku to report.

Hirotatsu, a retainer at the Kamisato estate, belittled the Traveler for hesitating to enter, then lost fairly and apologised. Ayaka, who had never before acted as ambassador for an event or fought in an elaborate costume, had worried about the role. After the match she said she had long wanted to spar with the Traveler.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 only the 3.4 edition (February 2023) is shown in canon. The Shogun's involvement remains limited to sending an envoy, and Ayaka is recorded as the most recent Archon's Emissary.

48.comment: Warrior's Spirit Swordfighting Exhibition: Archon's Emissary
48.content:
The Archon's Emissary is the figure in the exhibition match who stands in for the Almighty Shogun. In the legend, a familiar of the Shogun aided the champion in the duel against her; today the role is played by a true swordsman while a special envoy shows the Shogun's divine strength. In the 3.4 edition Kamisato Ayaka was the Emissary, fighting beside the champion against the Maguu Kengou. The idea of making Ayaka the Emissary came from Onodera, and she accepted it as an honour and a chance to promote the sword arts.

Ayaka was nervous because she had never been the public face of such an event and was to fight in a showy outfit. She had also considered writing to the Traveler for advice, but did not send the letter, saying she did not want to depend on the Traveler for everything.

49.comment: Warrior's Spirit Swordfighting Exhibition: Emissary outfit vote
49.content:
For the 3.4 edition, ballots were meant to let the public choose among four seasonal Inazuman styles for Ayaka's exhibition outfit. The ballot boxes for Warrior's Spirit and for the other events were mixed up by a staff member, Mizuta, while Onodera was away, so the announced results named outfits from popular novels instead: "The Case Files of Miss Orith" and "Pretty Please, Kitsune Guuji?". The Fontaine-style outfit of Miss Orith won by a wide margin. Rather than rerun the vote, Ayaka decided to wear it, reasoning that the public had taken the result as a pleasant surprise. The organisers tailored it to her measurements; it bore the Kamisato crest and allowed more freedom of movement than she had expected.

Ayaka saw it as a way to present something new in a traditional form, and as a way to fulfil her late mother's curiosity about other nations' clothing.

50.content:
Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri (also: Watatsumi Spirit Ritual, Watatsumi Mitama Omatsuri, Mitama Omatsuri): The Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri is a ritual of Watatsumi Island meant to stop its soil from bleaching and eroding. Local legend says the island's spirit is drawn down toward Enkanomiya; the ritual, performed with a Jade Coral Branch retrieved from the depths, calls the sunken spirit back. It is held only once every several centuries, and the Sangonomiya Shrine is responsible for it.

The affected soil turns white and is known as Holy Soil. The ritual only halts the erosion temporarily. Tsuyuko, the shrine maiden who raises the matter with the Traveler, is a descendant of Eboshi, a shrine maiden of Byakuyakoku's history, and is in charge of the ritual's affairs.

Practice: Per Tsuyuko, every few centuries, at a moment when the spirit veins flow smoothly, the barrier between Enkanomiya and Sangonomiya must be broken so someone can dive down and retrieve a Jade Coral Branch left by the Omikami (Orobashi). The branch is then used to perform the ritual, causing the sunken "spirit" to return and stopping the erosion. Entering Enkanomiya requires breaking the seals on four Goshou Rocks around the island (the Eye, Tooth, Fin and Tail) to gain Spirit Pearls, which open the fifth rock, the Heart; solving its puzzle yields the Key of the Moon-bathed Deep.

Near each of the four outer seals stands a tablet recording the ritual's matters, but the writing is badly worn after the ages and the rite for breaking the seals is now unknown to most people. The Jade Coral Branch was made from Orobashi's own body and also serves to suppress the Dragonheir of the Depths.

Explanations: Three accounts exist. The local legend: Enkanomiya's depths try to absorb the island's spirit, bleaching the soil and leaving it infertile. Tsuyuko, schooled at the Sumeru Akademiya, offers a scientific reading: seawater salinity and alkalinity leach nutrients, and the Jade Coral Branches, being full of Orobashi's power, replenish them.

The third account comes with Three Realms Gateway Offering (2.5), per the wiki's Holy Soil page. There the ritual's real purpose is to awaken Orobashi's second familiars, the Sangacorallia, which break the primitive elemental energy of the Light Realm into the milder energy of the Human Realm. The legend and Tsuyuko's science are therefore both partial, and canon does not reconcile the accounts.

History: In The Moon-Bathed Deep (2.1), Tsuyuko, a shrine maiden of the Sangonomiya Shrine, explains the ritual to the Traveler and why the Goshou Rock seals must be broken to reach Enkanomiya.

Per the Holy Soil page's account of the 2.5 event, the ritual, performed by Sangonomiya Kokomi, did not reverse the bleaching but halted it, which had never happened before. An investigation found that the Void Realm had invaded Enkanomiya and was suppressing interactions between the Light and Human Realms. The situation was resolved, but the supply of Jade Coral Branches was cut off because the vishaps rescued their sealed kin.

Scene use: Use it as a grave, communal rite tied to the island's survival and overseen by the Sangonomiya Shrine. Characters may disagree whether it works through myth or through soil chemistry.

Do not state a date or say the ritual is annual. Its effect is temporary, and it needs Orobashi's coral, whose source was cut off after the events of 2.5.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the ritual has been performed once in the Traveler's story, with Kokomi officiating, and only stopped the erosion. The vishaps' retrieval of their kin has cut off the source of Jade Coral Branches.

51.content: Five rocks around Watatsumi Island seal the entrance to Enkanomiya: Eye, Tooth, Fin, Tail and Heart. The first four are broken to retrieve Spirit Pearls, which unlock the Heart. The structure echoes other five-seal legends in Inazuma and Liyue.

52.content: Tsuyuko is a Sangonomiya Shrine maiden who studied at the Sumeru Akademiya, descended from the Byakuyakoku shrine maiden Eboshi, and is in charge of the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri.
